newsitem.title: USA: U.S Spot Products- Activity thins on NYMEX expiry.
newsitem.headline: U.S Spot Products- Activity thins on NYMEX expiry.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product trading quieted Friday afternoon as market players took to the sidelines ahead of the June NYMEX futures expiration.
Volatile movements on the NYMEX prevented traders from making deals, which kept most differentials near steady with levels seen earlier in the day.

On the NYMEX, June gasoline fell 1.47 cents by its expiration at te close while the July contract slipped a more modest 0.44 cent. June heating oil gained 0.49 cent as it left the board, and July heating dipped 0.18 cent.

The Midcontinent markets were quiet in late afternoon trade as many players focused on NYMEX activity ahead of the expiry. Most players were calling spot June barrels in both Chicago and Group Three since most of May has dried up.

In Chicago, a 50,000-barrel parcel for spot first cycle June was done at 3.50 cents over July NYMEX. 3.75 cent deals for smaller pieces were also heard done over the screen, about a quarter cent higher from this morning.
"It's all broker hype," said one trader. "It is pretty thin but a few people are just pushing it."

Group Three spot June unleaded was pegged 4.00/4.50 cents with a 4.00 cent deal heard done. Any months came in at 1.50/1.75 cents due to a narrowing spread between NYMEX July unleaded and the spot front month.
Activity in the gasoline market became very choppy during the afternoon because of the sharply narrowing spread between the June and July futures contracts, traders said.
"Its really hard to get a good assessment. We've seen a complete and utter collapse in the spread," one player said.

Gasoline for prompt delivery in the Harbor was quoted against the June futures Friday, though many traders took to the sidelines to wait and see how the market shapes up Monday, when the prompt market will key off the July contract, which ended Friday 0.87 cent under the June.

Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline was talked between 2.75 and 2.50 cents under the June NYMEX, according to traders, while prompt reformulated A2 barrels were talked 0.10 cent over the June futures.
However, reformulated A2 gasoline for delivery by June 10 changed hands at -0.25 cent under the July NYMEX.
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline inched higher by late Friday, with offers sitting at 1.30 cents under the July NYMEX price.

But traders said another burst of buying interest was likely early next week as a scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline hit. A scheduling deadline earlier this week on the Colonial, the main artery to the East Coast, sent gasoline differentials higher as players holding short positions chased barrels.
Prompt premium grade V1 gasoline changed hands as high as 5.90 cents above the M1 grade, trader said, up about 0.70 cent from Thursday's levels.
